children: WINNIPEG, Manitoba--Canola futures on the Intercontinental Exchange were lower Thursday morning amid mixed sentiment in comparable oils.
There was no canola trading Wednesday due to the National Day For Truth and Reconciliation.
Crude oil prices were rising on reports China will not export fuel in the month of October. Meanwhile, European rapeseed was also higher, but Chicago soyoil and Malaysian palm oil were down.
Most of the Prairies will see clear skies and daytime high temperatures in the teens Thursday. However, some parts of central Alberta and northern Saskatchewan will see some rain.
The Canadian dollar was down one-quarter of a U.S. cent from Tuesday's close. The Bank of Canada did not post a closing rate Wednesday.
Nearly 27,700 contracts were traded. Prices in Canadian dollars per metric ton as of 10:06 a.m. ET:
